title: Ear infection in a child: treatment and follow-up
what: The doctor checks your child's ear and decides how to treat the infection. Often this means pain relief and watching, and sometimes antibiotics.
why: When your child has an earache or a fever, sleeps badly, touches the ear, or has fluid coming out of the ear.
duration: the visit usually takes 15 to 30 minutes; an ear infection usually goes away in a few days
tell_doctor: When the pain started and if there was a fever
If there was discharge from the ear
If your child had ear infections before, and how often
What medicines you have already given

prepare.title: Pain relief
prepare.text: Before the visit, you can give a children's fever reducer in a dose based on weight. Tell the doctor what you gave.

prepare.title: Ear drops
prepare.text: Do not put anything in the ear before it is checked, especially if fluid is coming out.

prepare.title: Your child
prepare.text: Explain to your child that the doctor will look into the ear with a little light.

steps: The doctor asks about the symptoms
The ear is checked with an otoscope, a small light with a cone
The doctor looks at the throat and nose
The doctor explains the treatment plan and when to come back
feel: The exam does not hurt, but it may be uncomfortable if the ear is inflamed
Your child may be scared. Hold them on your lap
after: Give medicines exactly as the doctor prescribed
If an antibiotic is prescribed, do not stop it early
Keep the sore ear dry if fluid is coming out
Go to the follow-up visit as planned, even if your child is better
Hearing is checked if fluid stays in the ear
red_flags: A fever over 39°C, or a fever lasting more than 2 to 3 days
Swelling and redness behind the ear, or the ear sticks out
Your child is limp, has a severe headache, vomits, or has a stiff neck: call emergency services
Blood comes from the ear, or pus does not get less

faq.a: No. Many ear infections go away on their own. The doctor will decide based on age and symptoms.

faq.q: Can my child go outside with an ear infection?
faq.a: If there is no fever and your child feels well, usually yes. Ask the doctor.

reminders.text: Visit for your child's ear tomorrow. Write down what medicines you gave and the temperatures.
